assessmentSummary.identity: A planned linear acceleration followed by multi-step horizontal braking to a controlled bilateral static stick.
currentCardFindings: Two five-yard source definitions are exact distance variants of the generic Sprint-to-Stick Deceleration identity.
Five-yard and seven-to-ten-yard variants make entry-distance and braking-demand differences selectable without duplicating identities.
Four media links have current public oEmbed metadata only and remain unviewed candidates.

currentCardSnapshot.description: From the declared start, accelerate linearly through the exact approach distance, begin braking early enough to remain inside the marked zone, reduce velocity with organized steps, and finish in a stable bilateral athletic stance for the declared hold without turning, crossing, or running through. Approach distance, intent, braking-zone length, start stance, stop location, hold time, and recovery are recorded; stop before braking posture, foot placement, alignment, or confidence changes.

population.medicalScope: This card is not rehabilitation prescription or return-to-play clearance.

claims: Privacy-enhanced YouTube embed URLs can be constructed with youtube-nocookie.com.

The candidate watch URLs returned public oEmbed metadata on 2026-07-26; embed playback, full-video exact matching, cue and safety quality, captions, accessibility, reviewer identity, and approval remain unresolved.

evidence.sourceTitle: Biomechanical and Neuromuscular Performance Requirements of Horizontal Deceleration: A Review with Implications for Random Intermittent Multi-Directional Sports
claims: A planned straight-line acceleration transitions through a declared braking zone into a controlled bilateral athletic stick without a cut, turn, or reacceleration.
Five-yard and seven-to-ten-yard approaches are exact distance variants because they change entry speed and braking demand, not the accelerate-brake-stick sequence.

evidence.sourceTitle: Biomechanical and Neuromuscular Performance Requirements of Horizontal Deceleration: A Review with Implications for Random Intermittent Multi-Directional Sports
claims: The card combines linear locomotion and planned horizontal deceleration with a bilateral static finish.
Reactive cues, multidirectional cuts, backpedal entries, resistance, run-through finishes, and reacceleration remain separate definitions.

evidence.sourceTitle: Biomechanical and Neuromuscular Performance Requirements of Horizontal Deceleration: A Review with Implications for Random Intermittent Multi-Directional Sports
claims: Foot, ankle, knee, hip, and trunk actions absorb and redirect forward momentum through repeated braking contacts.
The listed muscles describe contributors to braking and stabilization without claiming isolation.

evidence.sourceTitle: Biomechanical and Neuromuscular Performance Requirements of Horizontal Deceleration: A Review with Implications for Random Intermittent Multi-Directional Sports
claims: Horizontal deceleration requires braking force, eccentric capacity, posture control, and multi-step organization; achieved entry velocity materially changes demand.
Exact card distances and dose thresholds are programming proposals rather than directly validated prescriptions.

evidence.sourceTitle: Biomechanical and Neuromuscular Performance Requirements of Horizontal Deceleration: A Review with Implications for Random Intermittent Multi-Directional Sports
claims: Complexity rises with approach speed, braking precision, shorter zones, and stricter stick criteria; physical difficulty rises with entry velocity, hard braking contacts, and density.
Overall exercise difficulty equals the greater of complexity and physical difficulty; exercise cards do not classify athlete proficiency.

evidence.sourceTitle: Biomechanical and Neuromuscular Performance Requirements of Horizontal Deceleration: A Review with Implications for Random Intermittent Multi-Directional Sports
claims: Short acceleration plus multi-step braking creates substantial eccentric and impact demand in the quadriceps, calves, gluteals, hamstrings, adductors, and trunk.
Track hard braking events and end before run-throughs, panic steps, twisting stops, alignment loss, or declining entry intent.

evidence.sourceTitle: Biomechanical and Neuromuscular Performance Requirements of Horizontal Deceleration: A Review with Implications for Random Intermittent Multi-Directional Sports
claims: Use a flat dry high-traction surface, measured approach and braking zones, clear runout, one-way lanes, and one athlete per lane.
Do not prescribe a speed or braking zone the athlete cannot repeatedly own.

evidence.sourceTitle: Biomechanical and Neuromuscular Performance Requirements of Horizontal Deceleration: A Review with Implications for Random Intermittent Multi-Directional Sports
claims: Use low numbers of fully recovered quality events, count hard braking contacts, and cap cumulative sprint, impact, and braking budgets.
The longer approach carries higher physical difficulty and requires repeatable success at the shorter variant first.

evidence.sourceTitle: Biomechanical and Neuromuscular Performance Requirements of Horizontal Deceleration: A Review with Implications for Random Intermittent Multi-Directional Sports
claims: Declare approach distance, start stance, entry intent, braking zone, finish mark, stick time, repetitions, lane order, and stop signal.
Accelerate straight, lower under control before the line, use ordered braking steps, stop without twisting, and hold the finish.

evidence.sourceTitle: Biomechanical and Neuromuscular Performance Requirements of Horizontal Deceleration: A Review with Implications for Random Intermittent Multi-Directional Sports
claims: Stop for symptoms, giving way, panic steps, run-through, twisting, repeated alignment loss, unsafe traffic, surface failure, or inability to stop inside the zone.
Reduce intent or extend the braking zone before adding repetitions.

evidence.sourceTitle: Biomechanical and Neuromuscular Performance Requirements of Horizontal Deceleration: A Review with Implications for Random Intermittent Multi-Directional Sports
claims: Use fresh in movement-learning or early output work before fatigue-heavy lower-body training.
Do not hide the braking dose inside conditioning or combine it with untracked high-speed running.

evidence.sourceTitle: Biomechanical and Neuromuscular Performance Requirements of Horizontal Deceleration: A Review with Implications for Random Intermittent Multi-Directional Sports
claims: Athlete support explains the lane, expected braking effort, self-checks, symptoms, confidence reporting, and how to reduce speed safely.
The athlete reports a run-through, twist, panic step, or fear rather than forcing the target speed.

evidence.sourceTitle: Biomechanical and Neuromuscular Performance Requirements of Horizontal Deceleration: A Review with Implications for Random Intermittent Multi-Directional Sports
claims: Coach support covers measuring zones, traffic flow, posture, braking onset, foot sequence, stop location, stick quality, and cumulative exposure.
The coach reduces intent or returns to the shorter distance when braking is not repeatable.

evidence.sourceTitle: Biomechanical and Neuromuscular Performance Requirements of Horizontal Deceleration: A Review with Implications for Random Intermittent Multi-Directional Sports
claims: Lower intent, a shorter approach, longer braking zone, fewer events, longer rest, and high-contrast markings can improve access.
A lower-speed eccentric stop is a distinct substitution when the athlete cannot yet own acceleration entry.

evidence.sourceTitle: Biomechanical and Neuromuscular Performance Requirements of Horizontal Deceleration: A Review with Implications for Random Intermittent Multi-Directional Sports
claims: Five-yard and seven-to-ten-yard approaches are variants; intent, zone length, stance, and hold time are modifiers.
Cuts, reactive cues, reacceleration, backpedal entries, resistance, and run-through finishes require separate definitions.

alternateAssessments.name: 5-Yard Acceleration Decel Stick
alternateAssessments.rationale: The five-yard source is an exact distance variant of this identity.

alternateAssessments.name: 5-Yard Accel to Decel Stick
alternateAssessments.rationale: Accel and decel abbreviate the same five-yard action.

alternateAssessments.name: Five-Yard Planned Sprint-to-Stick
alternateAssessments.rationale: Five yards constrains achieved entry speed and braking demand.

alternateAssessments.name: Seven-to-Ten-Yard Planned Sprint-to-Stick
alternateAssessments.rationale: A longer approach can raise entry velocity and braking demand.

alternateAssessments.name: Entry Intent or Braking-Zone Change
alternateAssessments.rationale: Intent, braking-zone length, start stance, and stick duration scale a declared distance variant.

alternateAssessments.name: Sprint to Cut or Turn
alternateAssessments.rationale: A directional turn changes plane, foot strategy, and exit.

alternateAssessments.name: Reactive Sprint-to-Stick
alternateAssessments.rationale: An unpredictable cue adds decision demand and response timing.

alternateAssessments.name: Sprint-to-Stick-to-Reacceleration
alternateAssessments.rationale: Reacceleration adds a second output phase after the stop.

alternateAssessments.name: Backpedal-to-Sprint-to-Stick
alternateAssessments.rationale: Backpedal entry adds a transition and different locomotor sequence.

alternateAssessments.name: Resisted or Partner-Pulled Sprint-to-Stick
alternateAssessments.rationale: External resistance changes mechanics, loading, equipment, and safety.

alternateAssessments.name: Run-Through Deceleration
alternateAssessments.rationale: A run-through finish omits the defining bilateral static stick.
